newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FULL TEXT - GENERALE BANK CEO CHAFFART STATEMENT.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - GENERALE BANK CEO CHAFFART STATEMENT.

text.p: Following is the full text of comments made by Ferdinand Chaffart, chief executive officer of Generale Bank at the presentation of the bank's 1996 earnings.
First comment Mr F. Chaffart
In terms of geographical distribution, our results break down as follows:

55% of our net profit is realised in Belgium (the inner circle of our international strategy). This covers the results of the parent company and its Belgian subsidiaries, including TCD, VIV, Synerfi, Alpha Life, Alpha Credit, Belgo-Factors and Eurolease. The portion of the group's net profit realised abroad increased from 40% in 1995 to 45% in 1996, mainly due to the fact that GBN and Fimagest were consolidated for the first time. The portion of net profit realised abroad was lower than as at 30 June 1996, due to a number of one-off technical factors relating to consolidation.
The neighbouring countries (the second circle) now account for more than 28% of net profit, compared to 18% in 1995:

- GBN's net profit for 1996 was some BFr 1,422 million (Fl 76.9 million). This represents an increase of 47.6% on the net profit for 1995. ROE increased from 5.6% in 1995 to 7.6% (after profit allocation) in 1996.
- Funds managed by Fimagest increased by 23%. As at the end of 1996 the amount managed stood at BFr 345 billion. ROE was 18.2%.
The third circle, which includes subsidiaries involved inter alia in private banking in Switzerland and Guernsey and our branches in Italy, Spain and Portugal, accounted for 3.4% of profit.

13.5% of net profit comes from the fourth circle (other continents). This circle includes our Hong Kong subsidiary, which accounts for more than 12% of the group's net profit and continues to post exceptionally good results.

Generale Belgian Bank is extending its commercial network. We now have 29 branch offices in Hong Kong. We have just received approval from the local monetary authorities to open another branch - alongside Generale Belgian Bank - with a new dealing room. This will make it possible for the Generale Bank group to have a round-the-clock presence on the financial markets.
Second comment Mr F. Chaffart
Asset Management
Asset management is one of Generale Bank group's priority business lines. It is increasingly developing across frontiers and world-wide.

At the end of 1996 assets managed by Generale Bank under discretionary or advisory management agreements totalled some BFr 1,700 billion, an increase of 20% on 1995. This includes collective investment undertakings, the portfolios of institutional and private investors and the portfolio managed by the bank's private banking department, its specialist subsidiaries and Banque Generale du Luxembourg. In CIUs alone the group managed an amount of BFr 981 billion at the end of 1996, which places us among the fifteen largest fund managers in Europe. With a market share of 23%, Generale Bank is also the Belgian market leader, managing a CIU portfolio of BFr 589 billion in 1996.
Over the past two years Generale Bank has taken a number of steps in order to extend its asset management activities within Europe and elsewhere in the world.

In 1995 the bank acquired Fimagest, a French company which manages assets on behalf of third parties. This offered the bank the opportunity of diversifying its distribution channels and attracting new customers, both individuals and institutions. Fimagest accounts for 30% of the group's CIU portfolio.

Along with its subsidiary Fimagest, Generale Bank acquired a 44.3% stake in the Paris-based company, FP Consult, early in 1997. The rest of the capital is held by UE-CIC (34.8%) and the management (20.9%).

FP Consult is a societe anonyme incorporated in 1989. It specialises in portfolio management and consultancy in portfolio management and financial engineering in France and elsewhere. Amongst other things, the company has developed specialist knowledge in the emerging countries market.

The group achieved a number of synergies at European level in 1996, by marketing Belgian products in Holland and France and selling Fimagest products in Belgium. For instance, "click" or "step-up" funds, which already existed in Belgium, France and Luxembourg, were successfully launched as a first by Generale Bank Nederland in July 1996. The products tailor- made for the group by SPAC, a subsidiary of Fimagest specialising in actuarial consultancy, also form part of this push for synergies.

In Hong Kong, Grand Generale Asia Ltd also specialises in fund management and securities brokerage. This company was set up in 1995 by Generale Bank and a subsidiary of the Guandong Development Bank, a Chinese commercial bank in Guangdong. At the end of 1996 Generale Bank increased its stake in this joint venture from 30% to 50%.
We are still looking to extend our asset management activities to the US - this would mainly be for institutional investors - and in Europe, more especially in the UK and Germany
Third comment Mr F. Chaffart
All in all 1996 was a successful year for our group. The highlights included:
- the ongoing profit growth: net profit has increased by an average 9.3% over the last five years;
- we achieved our strategic objective of ROE of at least 12.5% for the fifth year running;
- the consolidation of our recent acquisitions is starting to bear fruit;
- the success of the capital increase, whereby our group's capital adequacy rose;

- the gross dividend has increased by an average of 8.2% over the past five years; For the first time the share price passed the BFr 13,000 mark at closing on 6 March 1997. Between 1991 and 1996 the annual return on Generale Bank shares increased by 23.6%, compared to 21.8% for the Belgian banking sector (excluding Generale Bank) and 13.3% for the BEL 20-index.

Generale Bank is among the twenty-five largest banks in Europe. The banking sector in all countries is confronted with significant structural and operational changes. This process is set to accelerate and become more extensive in the years to come. The essential thing for our company is to become aware of and react to these changes in time. Only then will we be able to maintain our position in the fiercely competitive world of finance, including after monetary union. We will have to make qualitative and quantitative changes in employment practices due to technological developments and changes in customer behaviour and requirements.
I would also like to point out that:

firstly, between 1994 and 1996 we took on more than 2,500 people, 952 of these in 1996. Almost three-quarters of new staff on are unlimited contracts. 870 staff have taken early retirement - the bank meets most of the early retirement costs involved.

secondly, changes to the staff structure have meant that the average age of staff has been reduced by 12%. All new staff have taken part in higher education and almost 80% of them are employed in retail activities.
and finally, Generale Bank has fulfilled all its obligations under the government's measures for wage restraint. As a result of this wage restraint, it was possible to take on people.
I am sure that all these efforts will result in an improvement in our operating efficiency and reinforce our position against competition both within the banking sector and from other sectors.
END
